title: Load-balanced app with egress
description: Traffic enters through a load balancer, fans out to a scaled fleet, and leaves through a NAT gateway.

detail.role: Browsers and API clients calling the service.
detail.why: They are the source of all ingress traffic.

network.text: Only HTTPS is accepted at the edge.

detail.role: Terminates TLS and spreads requests across healthy app servers.
detail.why: One stable address in front of a fleet that changes size.
detail.tradeoff: Adds a hop and a per-hour plus per-request charge.

security.text: TLS ends here; the fleet only accepts traffic from the balancer.

cost.text: Billed per hour plus the capacity units actually used.

network.text: Listens on 443 and forwards to port 8080 on the fleet.

detail.role: Runs the application. Instances are interchangeable and spread across zones.
detail.why: A stateless fleet scales out under load and replaces failed instances.
detail.tradeoff: No local state, so sessions and uploads live elsewhere.

security.text: No public addresses; reachable only from the balancer.

cost.text: Pay per instance-hour; the floor is two instances.

network.text: Security group allows 8080 from the balancer only.

detail.role: Lets private instances start outbound connections without being reachable from outside.
detail.why: Instances need to call third-party APIs and fetch updates.
detail.tradeoff: Charged per hour and per GB processed.

security.text: Cannot be used to reach the instances from the internet.

cost.text: Data processing charges add up for chatty or large outbound traffic.

network.text: All outbound traffic passes here, so it can be logged and filtered.

detail.role: External service the app calls to take payments.
detail.why: Payments are not worth building in house.

network.text: Egress is limited to this provider's published addresses.

links.label: HTTPS
links.detail: Requests arrive over HTTPS and the response returns on the same connection.

links.label: Round robin
links.detail: The balancer picks a healthy instance for each request, using a health check on /healthz.

network.text: Forwarded to port 8080 on the fleet.

links.label: Read / write
links.detail: Application queries over a private connection.

security.text: No public route to the database.

links.label: Outbound calls
links.detail: Calls to external services leave through the NAT gateway.

network.text: The private route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 here.

links.label: HTTPS to provider
links.detail: The only way out to the provider; the request leaves the VPC from the NAT gateway's public address.

security.text: Only the provider's addresses are permitted.

cost.text: Outbound data transfer is billed per GB.

prose.text: Users reach a load balancer, which spreads requests over a scaled fleet in private subnets. The fleet reads a database and reaches a third-party API only through a NAT gateway.
